note: Additive alignment file for Agent 1's compiler schema (issue #22 comment, agent/modern-stdlib branch). Agent 1 added compiler/Analysis/libc_contracts.json (29 ordinary + checked APIs) and asked Agent 2 to emit libc/contracts with the keys params, ownership, transfer, extent, effects, failure, diagnostics and dynamic. This file mirrors those names/signatures for the ordinary C spellings implemented by the bundled cplus_* symbols; it does not replace the existing v1/v2 contract files. Names and parameter order match the standard C headers so Agent 1 can map format argument indices. 'dynamic' records checks this library actually performs at runtime (bounded recent-free caches, tracked remaining capacity, __builtin_object_size, unknown-capacity mode); it is NOT a claim of compile-time enforcement. Diagnostic strings are the CPLUS-SAFE-* categories requested by Agent 1. Agent 1's compiler file is not present on this branch, so this schema must be re-validated when PR #16 merges. Additive extension (2026-11-23, Agent 1 P0 integration): added vsnprintf and the checked allocators malloc_s/calloc_s/realloc_s/free_s/aligned_alloc_s (38 entries total). Two additive top-level keys, contract_semantics and implementation_symbols, document how the required semantic aspects map to the nine per-API keys and which concrete bundled symbol implements each contract; no per-API key was added or removed, so the nine-key schema is unchanged. Compiler consumption of this file CANNOT be proven on this branch: compiler/Analysis/libc_contracts.json is absent and the only machine check is tests/libc/test_compiler_contract_alignment.py (schema/name alignment), which does not load or exercise the compiler.
